purpose: reading-comprehension items; the contradicted item is composed by the pipeline from basis+alter and always shown with its label

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Shared T cell clonotypes across PBMC DNA, PBMC RNA and cfDNA repertoires were more frequently present after infusion than in baseline samples.
statements.evidence: Comparison between PBMC DNA, PBMC RNA, and circulating free DNA (cfDNA) repertoires demonstrated an increased presence of shared T cell clonotypes post-infusion when compared with baseline samples.
statements.note: The abstract reports an increased presence of shared clonotypes post-infusion relative to baseline across the three repertoire types.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Responders by RECIST criteria showed a higher abundance of TIL clonotypes in baseline and post-infusion PBMC DNA repertoires than non-responders.
statements.evidence: Higher abundance of TIL clonotypes in the PBMC baseline and post-infusion DNA T cell repertoires and the presence of shared DNA T cell clonotypes between timepoints was seen in responders when compared with non-responders according to RECIST criteria.
statements.note: The abstract reports higher, not lower, TIL clonotype abundance in baseline and post-infusion PBMC DNA repertoires of responders compared with non-responders.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with a higher number of TILs in the infusion product were more likely to respond to ACT.
statements.evidence: Conflicting evidence is observed in biomarkers such as the number of TILs in the infusion product, with some studies suggesting a relationship with response and others not.
statements.note: The infusion-product TIL count is mentioned only as a disputed biomarker from earlier studies; this study reports no result relating it to response.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nine melanoma patients, seven with cutaneous and two with mucosal disease, received TIL ACT following chemotherapeutic depletion.
statements.evidence: 9 patients with cutaneous (n = 7) or mucosal (n = 2) melanoma received TIL ACT after chemotherapeutic depletion.
statements.note: The abstract states the cohort was 9 patients, 7 with cutaneous and 2 with mucosal melanoma, treated with TIL ACT after chemotherapeutic depletion.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Zoantharian species living in the deep sea have larger genomes than those from intertidal zones.
statements.evidence: The order Zoantharia are benthic cnidarians found from intertidal zones to the deep sea, and some species are particularly abundant in coral reefs.
statements.note: Habitat range appears only as background; the abstract relates genome size to repeat content and never compares genome size between habitats.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genome size across the zoantharian dataset varied by up to 2.4-fold.
statements.evidence: The genome sizes in the dataset varied up to 2.4 fold magnitude.
statements.note: The abstract reports genome sizes in the dataset varying up to 2.4-fold.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In every species examined, LINEs and DNA transposons were the most abundant of the repeat elements that could be identified.
statements.evidence: In all species, long interspersed nuclear elements and DNA transposons were the most abundant identified elements.
statements.note: The abstract states that LINEs and DNA transposons were the most abundant identified elements in all species.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Genome size was significantly correlated with repeated DNA content across the zoantharian species sampled.
statements.evidence: Significant correlations between genome size, repeated DNA content and transposable elements, respectively (Pearson's correlation test R 2 = 0.47, p = 0.0016; R 2 = 0.22, p = 0.05) were found
statements.note: The abstract reports a significant correlation between genome size and repeated DNA content (R2 = 0.47, p = 0.0016).

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Patients whose treatment-naïve tumours carried the APOBEC or BRCA mutational signatures had significantly worse disease-specific survival.
statements.evidence: Mutational signatures SBS2/13 (APOBEC) and SBS3 (BRCA) were almost exclusively detected in private mutation populations of treatment-naïve tumours. Patients presenting these signatures had significantly worse disease specific survival.
statements.note: The abstract reports significantly worse, not better, disease-specific survival for patients whose tumours showed the APOBEC or BRCA signatures.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutational signatures linked to platinum-based chemotherapy, along with high platinum enrichment scores, were found only in post-treatment samples.
statements.evidence: mutational signatures associated with platinum-based chemotherapy treatment as well as high platinum enrichment scores were only detected in post-treatment samples.
statements.note: The abstract states platinum-associated signatures and high platinum enrichment scores were detected exclusively in post-treatment samples.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Post-treatment samples carried a higher total number of mutations than treatment-naïve samples.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, mutational signatures associated with platinum-based chemotherapy treatment as well as high platinum enrichment scores were only detected in post-treatment samples.
statements.note: The abstract describes which signatures appear after treatment but gives no comparison of total mutation counts between pre- and post-treatment samples.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The analysis used whole-genome sequencing of 59 treatment-naïve and 18 post-treatment samples from 29 patients with OAC.
statements.evidence: Whole-genome sequencing data from 59 treatment-naïve and 18 post-treatment samples from 29 OAC patients was analysed.
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly these sample counts: 59 treatment-naïve and 18 post-treatment samples from 29 patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The canT antiterminator was required for transcription of Tn916 genes once the element had excised from the host chromosome.
statements.evidence: we identified an element-encoded antiterminator (named canT for conjugation-associated antitermination) that is essential for transcription of Tn916 genes after excision of the element from the host chromosome.
statements.note: The abstract describes canT as essential for Tn916 gene transcription after excision.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Exposure to tetracycline increased canT-dependent transcription of Tn916 genes.
statements.evidence: Tn916, the founding member of a large family of integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs; aka conjugative transposons), confers tetracycline-resistance and is found in several Gram-positive bacterial species.
statements.note: Tetracycline is mentioned only as the resistance Tn916 confers; the abstract reports no experiment on tetracycline and antitermination.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss of the terminator near the end of Tn916 produced a fitness defect in the host cells.
statements.evidence: loss of the terminator caused a fitness defect for the host cells.
statements.note: The abstract states that losing the terminator caused a fitness defect for host cells.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: The canT antiterminator acted in an orientation-specific manner and functioned with heterologous promoters and terminators.
statements.evidence: We found that the antiterminator is orientation-specific, functions with heterologous promoters and terminators, is processive and is most likely a cis-acting RNA.
statements.note: The abstract reports the antiterminator is orientation-specific, not orientation-independent, while working with heterologous promoters and terminators.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with detectable pre-treatment ctDNA had a larger baseline tumour burden than patients without detectable ctDNA.
statements.evidence: Pre-treatment ctDNA was detectable in 19/40 (48%) patients.
statements.note: The abstract reports detection rates only; it never relates ctDNA status to tumour burden or stage within the cohort.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Of the 19 patients with detectable pre-treatment ctDNA, 17 (89%) zero-converted within six weeks of surgery and none of them recurred.
statements.evidence: Pre-treatment ctDNA was detectable in 19/40 (48%) patients. Among these, 17/19 (89%) zero-converted within six weeks of surgery and none recurred.
statements.note: The abstract states that none of the 17 patients who zero-converted within six weeks of surgery recurred.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: All four patients with positive post-surgery ctDNA recurred, giving 100% specificity but only 44% sensitivity for recurrence.
statements.evidence: Positive ctDNA post-surgery (N = 4), irrespective of pre-treatment ctDNA status, was 100% predictive of recurrence (sensitivity 44%, specificity 100%).
statements.note: The abstract reports post-surgery ctDNA positivity (N = 4) was 100% predictive of recurrence with 44% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ctDNA had already cleared before surgery in 7 of 9 (78%) patients who did not go on to recur.
statements.evidence: ctDNA cleared prior to surgery in 7/9 (78%) patients who did not recur
statements.note: The abstract reports pre-surgical ctDNA clearance in 7/9 (78%) of patients without recurrence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: KEGG enrichment identified three significant pathways: chemical carcinogenesis-receptor activation, the calcium signaling pathway and pathways in cancer.
statements.evidence: The significant pathways discovered using Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis were chemical carcinogenesis-receptor activation, calcium signaling pathway, and pathways in cancer.
statements.note: The abstract names exactly these three pathways as the significant KEGG enrichment results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Stigmasterol suppressed the malignant progression of U251 glioma cells in the in vitro assays.
statements.evidence: In vitro experimental results indicate that stigmasterol can inhibit the malignant progression of U251 cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports in vitro evidence that stigmasterol inhibits malignant progression of U251 cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Stigmasterol reduced glioma growth in a mouse xenograft model.
statements.evidence: In vitro experimental results indicate that stigmasterol can inhibit the malignant progression of U251 cells.
statements.note: Only cell-based in vitro assays are reported; no animal experiment is mentioned.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Data from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Human Protein Atlas linked high ADRB2 expression in glioma to a good outcome.
statements.evidence: Data from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Human Protein Atls databases indicate that ADRB1 and ADRB2 are expressed in glioma, and high expression of ADRB2 may predict a good outcome.
statements.note: The abstract reports that high ADRB2 expression may predict a good, not poor, outcome in glioma.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: For retrotransposons overlapping promoters and exons, methylation was inversely correlated with expression of the associated genes.
statements.evidence: Promoter- and exon-overlapping elements showed inverse correlations between methylation and gene expression, and enriched genes are involved in immune and transport pathways.
statements.note: The abstract reports inverse, not positive, correlations between methylation and gene expression for promoter- and exon-overlapping elements.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Blood leukocytes from mastitic cows showed the same retrotransposon hypermethylation pattern as milk somatic cells.
statements.evidence: DNA methylation profiles in milk somatic cells showed consistently high levels across retrotransposons, with widespread hypermethylation in cows with Staphylococcus aureus-induced subclinical mastitis.
statements.note: Methylation was profiled only in milk somatic cells; no other cell type or tissue is mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Retrotransposons made up roughly 40% of the bovine genome, with LINEs forming the largest share.
statements.evidence: Retrotransposons accounted for ~ 40% of the genome, with LINEs representing the largest fraction.
statements.note: The abstract gives ~40% genome coverage by retrotransposons, with LINEs the largest fraction.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The analysis found 20,839 differentially methylated retrotransposons, of which 3,306 overlapped differentially expressed genes.
statements.evidence: We identified 20,839 differentially methylated retrotransposons, 3,306 of which overlapped differentially expressed genes.
statements.note: The abstract gives these exact counts: 20,839 differentially methylated retrotransposons and 3,306 overlapping differentially expressed genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the bTMB-High cohort, the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval for response rate exceeded the prespecified 5% threshold, meeting the primary endpoint.
statements.evidence: In the bTMB-High cohort, the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval (CI) exceeded the prespecified 5% threshold, meeting the primary endpoint.
statements.note: The abstract states the bTMB-High cohort met its primary endpoint because the 90% CI lower bound exceeded 5%.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Patients whose ctDNA declined early, by week 3 of treatment, had longer progression-free survival.
statements.evidence: Early ctDNA decline at week 3 was associated with longer progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.29-0.87).
statements.note: The abstract reports early ctDNA decline at week 3 was associated with longer, not shorter, progression-free survival (HR 0.51).

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Higher baseline ctDNA concentrations were associated with a lower objective response rate, whereas baseline bTMB did not clearly separate responders from nonresponders.
statements.evidence: Baseline bTMB did not clearly distinguish responders from nonresponders, whereas higher baseline ctDNA concentrations were associated with a lower ORR.
statements.note: The abstract reports both: baseline bTMB did not clearly distinguish responders, while higher baseline ctDNA concentration went with lower ORR.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose high bTMB was matched by high tissue TMB responded better than those with discordant tissue TMB.
statements.evidence: Tissue-based tumor mutational burden (TMB) is a biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitors; however, data on circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based blood TMB (bTMB) are limited.
statements.note: Tissue TMB appears only as background; the study reports no tissue TMB measurements or concordance analysis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The SPOT-MAS assay detected hormone receptor-positive breast cancers at a higher rate than triple-negative tumours.
statements.evidence: However, the detection of breast cancer, particularly in early stages, is challenging due to the low amount of ctDNA and heterogeneity of molecular subtypes.
statements.note: Subtype heterogeneity is named as a challenge; the abstract reports no sensitivity broken down by molecular subtype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The combined model reached an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI 0.87-0.95) and detected 65% of breast cancers at 96% specificity.
statements.evidence: achieving an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.87-0.95), a sensitivity of 65% at 96% specificity.
statements.note: The abstract gives AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.87-0.95) with 65% sensitivity at 96% specificity for the combination model.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: A model combining methylation, copy number and end-motif features performed better than models built from any single feature type.
statements.evidence: the combination model outperformed base models built from individual features
statements.note: The abstract reports that the combination model outperformed, not underperformed, the base models built from individual features.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Plasma cfDNA of breast cancer patients showed distinct genome-wide methylation, copy number alteration and 4-mer end-motif profiles.
statements.evidence: We identified distinct profiles of genome-wide methylation changes (GWM), copy number alterations (CNA), and 4-nucleotide oligomer (4-mer) end motifs (EM) in cfDNA of breast cancer patients.
statements.note: The abstract reports distinct GWM, CNA and 4-mer end-motif profiles in cfDNA of breast cancer patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The eight most altered genes with pathogenic or oncogenic mutations were TP53, SMAD4, ERBB3, KRAS, ARID1A, PIK3CA, RB1 and AXIN1.
statements.evidence: Our findings focused on the eight most altered genes with pathogenic and oncogenic mutations: TP53, SMAD4, ERBB3, KRAS, ARID1A, PIK3CA, RB1, and AXIN1.
statements.note: The abstract lists exactly these eight genes as the most altered with pathogenic and oncogenic mutations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with TP53-mutated tumours had shorter survival than those with TP53 wild-type tumours.
statements.evidence: Our findings focused on the eight most altered genes with pathogenic and oncogenic mutations: TP53, SMAD4, ERBB3, KRAS, ARID1A, PIK3CA, RB1, and AXIN1.
statements.note: The abstract lists frequently mutated genes but reports no survival or outcome analysis for any gene.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Certain mutational signatures, including COSMIC 1, 6, 18 and 29, were related to patient age and tobacco smoking.
statements.evidence: our research related certain mutational signatures, such as cosmic 1, cosmic 6, and cosmic 18, 29, to known characteristics including patient age and tobacco smoking
statements.note: The abstract relates these signatures to patient age and tobacco smoking; alcohol is not mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes carrying pathogenic SNVs were enriched in oncogenic signalling pathways, particularly RTK-RAS, WNT and TP53.
statements.evidence: Genes with pathogenic single nucleotide variations (SNVs) were enriched in oncogenic signaling pathways, particularly RTK-RAS, WNT, and TP53 pathways.
statements.note: The abstract reports enrichment of pathogenic SNV genes in the RTK-RAS, WNT and TP53 pathways.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Across the tools evaluated, precision and recall varied substantially.
statements.evidence: Our results show significant differences in calling strategies, leading to substantial variation in precision, recall, and the spectrum of TE families detected across tools.
statements.note: The abstract reports substantial variation in precision and recall across tools, not near-identical performance.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The benchmark also exposed differences between TE calls derived from short-read and from long-read data.
statements.evidence: Our benchmark also displays the differences between short-read and long-read calls, highlighting the importance of appropriate method selection.
statements.note: The abstract states the benchmark displays differences between short-read and long-read calls.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The tools' computational requirements were documented alongside their strengths and limitations.
statements.evidence: Strengths and limitations of different tools have been highlighted in depth as well as their computational requirements
statements.note: The abstract says strengths, limitations and computational requirements of the tools were highlighted in depth.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The long-read tools detected Alu insertions more reliably than LINE-1 or SVA insertions.
statements.evidence: Our results show significant differences in calling strategies, leading to substantial variation in precision, recall, and the spectrum of TE families detected across tools.
statements.note: The abstract reports that the spectrum of TE families detected varied across tools but gives no family-level accuracy ranking.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell DNA sequencing identified two low-frequency mutation clones, in NLRP5 and HMMR, with important roles in CSCC clonal evolution.
statements.evidence: scDNA-seq identified two low-frequency mutation clones, NLRP5 and HMMR, which play important roles in the clonal evolution of CSCC.
statements.note: The abstract names NLRP5 and HMMR as two low-frequency clones identified by scDNA-seq with roles in clonal evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Missense mutations were the predominant mutation type among the somatic mutations found by bulk sequencing of the CSCC tumours.
statements.evidence: Bulk sequencing revealed a diverse spectrum of somatic mutations in CSCC tumors, with missense mutations being predominant.
statements.note: The abstract states missense mutations were predominant in the bulk sequencing results.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Mutation frequencies of HRAS, TTN, MUC16 and MUC4 differed significantly between this Chinese cohort and Korean and Caucasian populations.
statements.evidence: However, the mutation frequencies of HRAS, TTN, MUC16 and MUC4 were significantly different from the Korean and Caucasian populations.
statements.note: The abstract reports these four genes' mutation frequencies were significantly different from Korean and Caucasian populations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Cumulative UV exposure history was associated with NOTCH1 mutation status in these patients.
statements.evidence: Comparative analysis revealed associations between specific gene mutations and clinical characteristics such as tumor stage and patient sex.
statements.note: The clinical characteristics examined were tumour stage and patient sex; UV exposure is not mentioned anywhere in the abstract.
